在当前已有删除请求受理、分页查询、状态与执行日志 HTTP 入口，以及存储层 reconcile_execution 确定语义的基线上，我这次只开放单请求执行对账 HTTP 功能，不改其他入口和底层状态机。公开入口为 POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile，目标租户沿用现有 X-Tenant-Id 或 tenant_id 解析规则。入口不接收业务参数，Content-Length 缺省或为 0 表示无正文，其他正文返回 400 invalid_request。成功时返回 200 和与状态查询同形的单行 JSON，字段只有 request_id、status、created_at，为对账后当前记录，不暴露主体、范围、幂等键、worker、凭证或尝试明细。
鉴权配置兼容 request:submit、request:read，并新增 request:reconcile，旧配置拒绝规则不变。启用鉴权时，缺失或未知 Bearer 凭证返回 401 unauthorized，缺少 request:reconcile 角色或租户不一致返回 403 forbidden；关闭鉴权时不做角色门禁。目标租户缺失或空返回 400 invalid_request；请求编号格式非法、未知、尚未受理或跨租户统一返回 404 not_found。存储层参数错误返回 400 invalid_request，存储故障或损坏返回 503 storage_unavailable。该资源的非 POST 方法返回 405 method_not_allowed 并带 Allow: POST，HEAD 不返回正文；更深路径仍是 404 not_found。错误正文只含 error 字段，响应和日志不泄露秘密、SQL 或文件路径。
不新增批量对账 HTTP 入口；现有请求入口的方法、鉴权、状态码、JSON 字段顺序、分页语义和兼容行为保持不变，也不改写 reconcile_execution 既有领取、租约、补写执行记录、终态保持和跨重启语义。重复调用不得改变稳定终态、历史尝试或既有时间，并发调用由存储层原子提交决定唯一结果，失败调用不得留下半成响应或额外业务记录。

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

1	"""HTTP layer for deletion-request acceptance, lookup and observation.
2	
3	The service exposes five business endpoints:
4	
5	* ``POST /requests`` -- accept a deletion request for a tenant. The JSON
6	  body must carry non-empty ``tenant_id``, ``subject_id`` and
7	  ``idempotency_key`` strings plus a non-empty ``scopes`` array of
8	  distinct non-empty strings.
9	* ``GET /requests`` -- the tenant-scoped, paginated listing of accepted
10	  requests. The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule;
11	  the optional ``status`` (comma-separated distinct lifecycle statuses),
12	  ``created_from`` (inclusive) and ``created_to`` (exclusive) RFC3339 UTC
13	  bounds, ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100) query
14	  parameters filter and page the result. The single-line JSON body
15	  carries exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``; each item carries
16	  exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in ascending
17	  acceptance order, and ``next_cursor`` is the opaque continuation value
18	  or ``null`` at the end of the listing. Any other query parameter, a
19	  duplicated ``status`` value or a malformed filter answers 400.
20	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}`` -- return the accepted request's
21	  receipt, scoped to the tenant identified by the ``X-Tenant-Id`` header
22	  (or a ``tenant_id`` query parameter). The receipt is the record frozen
23	  at acceptance time and always reports ``accepted``; it never changes
24	  when the request's status subsequently advances.
25	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/status`` -- read-only observation of the
26	  request's current state. The single-line JSON body carries exactly
27	  ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in that order; ``status``
28	  is the latest persisted state while ``created_at`` stays the original
29	  acceptance time.
30	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/execution-log`` -- read-only observation
31	  of the request's execution attempts. The single-line JSON body carries
32	  exactly ``request_id`` and ``attempts``; attempts are ordered by
33	  ``attempt_number`` starting at 1 and each entry carries exactly
34	  ``attempt_number``, ``claimed_at``, ``lease_expires_at``, ``result``
35	  and ``completed_at``. An unfinished attempt has ``null`` ``result`` and
36	  ``completed_at``; a finished attempt carries its stored ``completed``
37	  or ``failed`` result and completion time.
38	
39	The observation endpoints never advance state, create an attempt or
40	write any bookkeeping; they only read persisted rows, so their answers
41	match the persisted records after a restart. They never expose a lease
42	credential, worker identity, subject, scope or any other request field.
43	
44	Status advancement (:meth:`RequestStore.transition`), the execution
45	orchestration (:meth:`RequestStore.claim_next`,
46	:meth:`RequestStore.finish_claim`, :meth:`RequestStore.renew_lease`,
47	:meth:`RequestStore.transfer_claim`,
48	:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`,
49	:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_batch`,
50	:meth:`RequestStore.migrate_execution_leases`) and the deletion receipts
51	(:meth:`RequestStore.generate_receipt`,
52	:meth:`RequestStore.verify_receipt`,
53	:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_receipt_key`) and the anchor capability
54	(:meth:`RequestStore.verify_chain`,
55	:meth:`RequestStore.diagnose_chain`,
56	:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_anchor_key`) and the read-only batched
57	audit inspection (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection` and
58	:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection_summary`) exist only on
59	the storage layer and are deliberately not exposed over HTTP: over HTTP
60	the service opens request acceptance, the acceptance-receipt lookup, the
61	read-only tenant-scoped listing and the two read-only observation reads
62	described above. The current-status
63	lookup (:meth:`RequestStore.get_status`), the tenant-scoped listing
64	(:meth:`RequestStore.list_requests`) and the execution log
65	(:meth:`RequestStore.get_execution_log`) back the read-only
66	endpoints but remain storage-layer methods as well.
67	
68	Success responses are a single line of JSON followed by a trailing
69	newline. Acceptance, receipt lookup and the status read render exactly
70	``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` (in that order); the same
71	idempotent request and every lookup return byte-identical bodies. The
72	execution-log read renders exactly ``request_id`` and ``attempts``. The
73	listing read renders exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``, each item
74	rendering exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``.
75	Error responses are single-line JSON objects with exactly one key,
76	``error``, holding a stable error code:
77	
78	``invalid_request`` (400), ``unauthorized`` (401), ``forbidden``
79	(403), ``idempotency_conflict`` (409), ``not_found`` (404),
80	``method_not_allowed`` (405) and ``storage_unavailable`` (503).
81	
82	Optional token authentication and role-based access control can be
83	enabled by passing an auth configuration (see :func:`load_auth_config`)
84	to :func:`build_server` / :func:`make_handler`. Without it the service
85	keeps the unauthenticated contract described above. When enabled every
86	matched business request must present ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``
87	for a configured principal: a missing/malformed/unknown token answers
88	``401 unauthorized`` and a principal lacking the role required by the
89	endpoint, or acting on a tenant other than its own ``tenant_id``,
90	answers ``403 forbidden``. ``POST /requests`` requires
91	``request:submit`` and the target tenant is the body's ``tenant_id``;
92	each of the four GET endpoints requires ``request:read`` and the target
93	tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule. Authentication
94	runs after path/method routing (unknown paths stay 404, unsupported
95	methods stay 405) but before payload validation and any storage access.
96	Tokens, roles and the configuration never enter a response, a raised
97	exception message, a log record, the database or any stored artifact.
98	
99	No subject, scope, idempotency key, lease credential, worker identity,
100	database error text, SQL statement or filesystem path is ever placed in
101	a response, a log record or a raised exception message.
102	"""
103	
104	from __future__ import annotations
105	
106	import json
107	import logging
108	import re
109	import sqlite3
110	import threading
111	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
112	from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit
113	
114	from .requests import IdempotencyConflict, RequestNotFound, RequestStore
115	
116	__all__ = [
117	    "build_server",
118	    "make_handler",
119	    "DeferredRequestStore",
120	    "AuthConfig",
121	    "AuthConfigError",
122	    "load_auth_config",
123	]
124	
125	_log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
126	
127	_COLLECTION_PATH = "/requests"
128	_ITEM_PATH_PREFIX = "/requests/"
129	_STATUS_RESOURCE = "status"
130	_EXECUTION_LOG_RESOURCE = "execution-log"
131	_TENANT_HEADER = "X-Tenant-Id"
132	_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER = "Authorization"
133	_BEARER_PREFIX = "Bearer "
134	
135	# Reject oversized request bodies before they reach the database layer.
136	_MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB
137	
138	_ROLE_SUBMIT = "request:submit"
139	_ROLE_READ = "request:read"
140	_ALLOWED_ROLES = frozenset({_ROLE_SUBMIT, _ROLE_READ})
141	
142	# Terminal attempt results, mirrored from the execution state machine so a
143	# corrupt or substituted store can never serialise another value.
144	_TERMINAL_RESULTS = frozenset({"completed", "failed"})
145	
146	# The request lifecycle statuses the tenant-scoped listing accepts in its
147	# ``status`` filter and may serialise in an item.
148	_REQUEST_STATUSES = frozenset({"accepted", "processing", "completed", "failed"})
149	
150	# The query parameters the GET /requests listing understands; anything
151	# else is an invalid request.
152	_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS = frozenset(
153	    {"tenant_id", "status", "created_from", "created_to", "cursor", "limit"}
154	)
155	_LIST_LIMIT_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9]+$")
156	
157	_UUID_RE = re.compile(
158	    r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-"
159	    r"[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$"
160	)
161	
162	_INVALID_REQUEST = "invalid_request"
163	_UNAUTHORIZED = "unauthorized"
164	_FORBIDDEN = "forbidden"
165	_NOT_FOUND = "not_found"
166	_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED = "method_not_allowed"
167	_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT = "idempotency_conflict"
168	_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE = "storage_unavailable"
169	
170	
171	class _BadRequest(Exception):
172	    """Internal signal for malformed or rejected client input."""
173	
174	
175	class _StorageUnavailable(Exception):
176	    """Internal signal: the backing database cannot be opened or used."""
177	
178	
179	class AuthConfigError(Exception):
180	    """The auth configuration file is missing, unreadable or invalid.
181	
182	    The message is a fixed marker; it never quotes the offending token,
183	    path or configuration content.
184	    """
185	
186	
187	class AuthConfig:
188	    """Parsed, immutable bearer-token principals for RBAC.
189	
190	    Principals map a non-empty bearer token to their tenant id and a set
191	    of roles. Tokens and roles are kept in process memory only and are
192	    never logged or persisted by this module.
193	    """
194	
195	    def __init__(self, principals: list[dict]):
196	        # ``principals`` has already passed :func:`load_auth_config`; copy
197	        # into an immutable token -> (tenant_id, frozenset(roles)) map.
198	        by_token: dict[str, tuple[str, frozenset[str]]] = {}
199	        for principal in principals:
200	            by_token[principal["token"]] = (
201	                principal["tenant_id"],
202	                frozenset(principal["roles"]),
203	            )
204	        self._by_token = by_token
205	
206	    def authenticate(self, token: str) -> tuple[str, frozenset[str]] | None:
207	        """Return ``(tenant_id, roles)`` for *token*, or ``None`` if unknown."""
208	        return self._by_token.get(token)
209	
210	
211	def load_auth_config(path: str) -> AuthConfig:
212	    """Read and validate the auth configuration file once, at startup.
213	
214	    The file must be a UTF-8 JSON object with a ``principals`` array;
215	    each principal is an object carrying non-empty ``token`` and
216	    ``tenant_id`` strings plus a non-empty ``roles`` array of distinct
217	    values drawn from ``request:submit`` and ``request:read``. Tokens
218	    must be unique across principals. Any deviation -- including an
219	    unreadable or non-UTF-8 file, malformed JSON, a missing ``principals``
220	    key or a principal missing/typing-wrong one of the required keys --
221	    raises :class:`AuthConfigError` so the caller can refuse to bind.
222	    """
223	    # Suppress exception chaining ("from None"): the underlying OSError
224	    # carries the filesystem path and a decode/JSON error may quote file
225	    # content, neither of which may reach a raised exception message.
226	    try:
227	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
228	            raw = handle.read()
229	    except OSError:
230	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid") from None
231	    try:
232	        parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
233	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
234	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid") from None
235	
236	    principals = _validate_auth_config(parsed)
237	    return AuthConfig(principals)
238	
239	
240	def _validate_auth_config(parsed: object) -> list[dict]:
241	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict) or "principals" not in parsed:
242	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
243	    raw_principals = parsed["principals"]
244	    if not isinstance(raw_principals, list):
245	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
246	
247	    principals: list[dict] = []
248	    seen_tokens: set[str] = set()
249	    for entry in raw_principals:
250	        # Only the three specified keys are validated; their presence,
251	        # types and value domains are mandatory.
252	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not {
253	            "token",
254	            "tenant_id",
255	            "roles",
256	        } <= set(entry):
257	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
258	        token = entry["token"]
259	        tenant_id = entry["tenant_id"]
260	        roles = entry["roles"]
261	        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
262	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
263	        if not isinstance(tenant_id, str) or not tenant_id:
264	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
265	        if not isinstance(roles, list) or not roles:
266	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
267	        if not all(isinstance(role, str) for role in roles):
268	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
269	        if len(set(roles)) != len(roles) or not set(roles) <= _ALLOWED_ROLES:
270	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
271	        if token in seen_tokens:
272	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
273	        seen_tokens.add(token)
274	        principals.append(
275	            {"token": token, "tenant_id": tenant_id, "roles": roles}
276	        )
277	    return principals
278	
279	
280	class DeferredRequestStore:
281	    """Lazily (re)initialising :class:`RequestStore` wrapper.
282	
283	    Opening the store and creating the required tables is attempted once
284	    at construction (service startup); if the database cannot be created
285	    -- an unwritable path, a corrupt file, an I/O error -- startup still
286	    succeeds and every business call retries initialization, failing the
287	    single request with the stable ``storage_unavailable`` outcome. This
288	    keeps "database cannot be created" indistinguishable from "database
289	    became unusable": both answer HTTP 503 instead of taking the whole
290	    service down, and a storage path repaired at runtime heals on the
291	    next request without a restart.
292	    """
293	
294	    def __init__(self, db_path: str):
295	        self._db_path = db_path
296	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
297	        self._store: RequestStore | None = None
298	        try:
299	            self._store = RequestStore(db_path)
300	        except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError):
301	            _log.warning("storage unavailable at startup")
302	
303	    def _ready(self) -> RequestStore:
304	        if self._store is not None:
305	            return self._store
306	        with self._lock:
307	            if self._store is None:
308	                try:
309	                    self._store = RequestStore(self._db_path)
310	                except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError):
311	                    raise _StorageUnavailable
312	            return self._store
313	
314	    def submit(self, tenant_id, subject_id, scopes, idempotency_key):
315	        return self._ready().submit(tenant_id, subject_id, scopes, idempotency_key)
316	
317	    def get(self, tenant_id, request_id):
318	        return self._ready().get(tenant_id, request_id)
319	
320	    def get_status(self, tenant_id, request_id):
321	        # Serves the read-only GET /requests/{request_id}/status endpoint.
322	        return self._ready().get_status(tenant_id, request_id)
323	
324	    def list_requests(
325	        self,
326	        tenant_id,
327	        statuses=None,
328	        created_from=None,
329	        created_to=None,
330	        cursor=None,
331	        limit=None,
332	    ):
333	        # Serves the read-only GET /requests tenant-scoped listing.
334	        return self._ready().list_requests(
335	            tenant_id, statuses, created_from, created_to, cursor, limit
336	        )
337	
338	    def transition(self, tenant_id, request_id, target_status):
339	        # Storage-layer only; not routed over HTTP, but proxied so this
340	        # wrapper stays a faithful RequestStore substitute.
341	        return self._ready().transition(
342	            tenant_id, request_id, target_status
343	        )
344	
345	    def claim_next(self, tenant_id, worker_id, lease_seconds):
346	        # Execution orchestration is storage-layer only; like the status
347	        # machine it is never routed over HTTP.
348	        return self._ready().claim_next(tenant_id, worker_id, lease_seconds)
349	
350	    def finish_claim(self, tenant_id, request_id, claim_token, result):
351	        return self._ready().finish_claim(
352	            tenant_id, request_id, claim_token, result
353	        )
354	
355	    def renew_lease(self, tenant_id, request_id, claim_token, lease_seconds):
356	        # Lease renewal is storage-layer only; like the rest of the
357	        # execution orchestration it is never routed over HTTP.
358	        return self._ready().renew_lease(
359	            tenant_id, request_id, claim_token, lease_seconds
360	        )
361	
362	    def transfer_claim(self, tenant_id, request_id, claim_token, lease_seconds):
363	        # The secure lease handover is storage-layer only; like the rest
364	        # of the execution orchestration it is never routed over HTTP.
365	        return self._ready().transfer_claim(

422	def build_server(
423	    store,
424	    host: str = "127.0.0.1",
425	    port: int = 8080,
426	    auth: AuthConfig | None = None,
427	) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
428	    """Build (but do not start) the threaded HTTP server bound to *host*:*port*.
429	
430	    With *auth* ``None`` (the default) the server keeps its
431	    unauthenticated contract; pass a loaded :class:`AuthConfig` to
432	    require bearer-token authentication and RBAC on the business
433	    endpoints.
434	    """
435	    handler = make_handler(store, auth)
436	    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), handler)
437	    # Worker threads must not keep the process alive on shutdown.
438	    server.daemon_threads = True
439	    return server

442	def make_handler(
443	    store: RequestStore,
444	    auth: AuthConfig | None = None,
445	) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
446	    """Build a handler class closed over *store* and optional *auth*."""
447	
448	    class _DeletionRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
449	        protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
450	        # Do not advertise the runtime version.
451	        server_version = "forgetting-evidence/0.1"
452	        sys_version = ""
453	
454	        def version_string(self) -> str:  # type: ignore[override]
455	            # BaseHTTPRequestHandler joins server/sys versions with a
456	            # space; with an empty sys version that leaves a trailing
457	            # space, so render the fixed token verbatim.
458	            return self.server_version
459	
460	        # -- routing ---------------------------------------------------
461	
462	        def _route(self) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
463	            path = urlsplit(self.path).path
464	            if path == _COLLECTION_PATH:
465	                return "collection", None
466	            if path.startswith(_ITEM_PATH_PREFIX):
467	                segment = path[len(_ITEM_PATH_PREFIX) :]
468	                # Empty or nested segments do not name a request.
469	                if segment and "/" not in segment:
470	                    return "item", segment
471	                # The two read-only observability sub-resources live under
472	                # a request id: /requests/{id}/status and
473	                # /requests/{id}/execution-log. Deeper nesting or any other
474	                # suffix stays an unknown path (404).
475	                if "/" in segment:
476	                    item_id, suffix = segment.split("/", 1)
477	                    if item_id and "/" not in suffix:
478	                        if suffix == _STATUS_RESOURCE:
479	                            return "status", item_id
480	                        if suffix == _EXECUTION_LOG_RESOURCE:
481	                            return "execution_log", item_id
482	            return None, None
483	
484	        # -- method entry points --------------------------------------
485	
486	        def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
487	            self._guard(self._handle_post)
488	
489	        def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
490	            self._guard(self._handle_get)
491	
492	        def do_HEAD(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
493	            # HEAD receives the same 405/404 routing as other unsupported
494	            # verbs, with headers but no body.
495	            self._guard(lambda: self._handle_unsupported_method(headless=True))
496	
497	        def do_PUT(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
498	            self._guard(self._handle_unsupported_method)
499	
500	        def do_DELETE(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
501	            self._guard(self._handle_unsupported_method)
502	
503	        def do_PATCH(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
504	            self._guard(self._handle_unsupported_method)
505	
506	        def do_OPTIONS(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
507	            self._guard(self._handle_unsupported_method)
508	
509	        def handle_expect_100(self) -> bool:  # type: ignore[override]
510	            # Honour "Expect: 100-continue" so clients (e.g. curl with a
511	            # large body) send the payload instead of waiting for a
512	            # 100-continue that never arrives.
513	            return True
514	
515	        def _guard(self, handler) -> None:
516	            try:
517	                handler()
518	            except _BadRequest:
519	                self._safe_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
520	            except Exception:
521	                # A defect in request handling must surface as the
522	                # stable storage code only; never let http.server print a
523	                # traceback (which could quote SQL or paths) to stderr.
524	                _log.warning("request failed: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
525	                self._safe_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
526	
527	        def _handle_unsupported_method(self, headless: bool = False) -> None:
528	            kind, _ = self._route()
529	            if kind is None:
530	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND, headless=headless)
531	            else:
532	                # The collection accepts POST (acceptance) and GET (the
533	                # tenant-scoped listing); the item and both read-only
534	                # sub-resources are GET-only.
535	                allowed = "GET, POST" if kind == "collection" else "GET"
536	                self._reply_error(
537	                    405, _METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, allowed=allowed, headless=headless
538	                )
539	
540	        # -- authentication / authorization ----------------------------
541	
542	        def _authorize(self, required_role: str) -> tuple[str, frozenset[str]] | None:
543	            """Authenticate the bearer token and check *required_role*.
544	
545	            Returns the principal's ``(tenant_id, roles)`` on success.
546	            Replies ``401 unauthorized`` for a missing, malformed or
547	            unknown credential and ``403 forbidden`` when the role is
548	            absent; returns ``None`` in either case. No token material is
549	            ever logged or quoted in the response.
550	            """
551	            if auth is None:
552	                # Unauthenticated deployment: no principal and no gate.
553	                return ("", frozenset())
554	            header = self.headers.get(_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER)
555	            if header is None or not header.startswith(_BEARER_PREFIX):
556	                self._auth_rejected(401, _UNAUTHORIZED)
557	                return None
558	            token = header[len(_BEARER_PREFIX) :]
559	            if not token:
560	                self._auth_rejected(401, _UNAUTHORIZED)
561	                return None
562	            principal = auth.authenticate(token)
563	            if principal is None:
564	                self._auth_rejected(401, _UNAUTHORIZED)
565	                return None
566	            tenant_id, roles = principal
567	            if required_role not in roles:
568	                self._auth_rejected(403, _FORBIDDEN)
569	                return None
570	            return tenant_id, roles
571	
572	        def _auth_rejected(self, status: int, code: str) -> None:
573	            # A rejected POST has not consumed its request body, so the
574	            # connection cannot serve another pipelined request; close it
575	            # after the error to keep keep-alive framing intact.
576	            if self.command == "POST":
577	                self.close_connection = True
578	            self._reply_error(status, code)
579	
580	        def _tenant_allowed(
581	            self, principal_tenant: str, target_tenant: str
582	        ) -> bool:
583	            if auth is None:
584	                return True
585	            if target_tenant != principal_tenant:
586	                self._reply_error(403, _FORBIDDEN)
587	                return False
588	            return True
589	
590	        def _handle_post(self) -> None:
591	            kind, _ = self._route()
592	            if kind is None:
593	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
594	                return
595	            if kind != "collection":
596	                self._reply_error(405, _METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, allowed="GET")
597	                return
598	            # Authentication precedes payload validation and storage.
599	            principal = self._authorize(_ROLE_SUBMIT)
600	            if principal is None:
601	                return
602	            payload = self._read_json_object()
603	            tenant_id = _require_string(payload, "tenant_id")
604	            # The body's tenant is the authorization target; a principal
605	            # may only submit for its own tenant.
606	            if not self._tenant_allowed(principal[0], tenant_id):
607	                return
608	            subject_id = _require_string(payload, "subject_id")
609	            idempotency_key = _require_string(payload, "idempotency_key")
610	            scopes = _require_scopes(payload)
611	            try:
612	                receipt = store.submit(
613	                    tenant_id, subject_id, scopes, idempotency_key
614	                )
615	            except ValueError:
616	                # Defence in depth: the HTTP validation above is
617	                # authoritative, but a rejected store call writes nothing
618	                # and maps to the same client error.
619	                self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
620	                return
621	            except IdempotencyConflict:
622	                self._reply_error(409, _IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT)
623	                return
624	            except _StorageUnavailable:
625	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
626	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
627	                return
628	            except (sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError, OSError):
629	                # The store deliberately raises fixed-text RuntimeErrors;
630	                # sqlite/OSError text (locks, malformed images, paths)
631	                # must never reach the client.
632	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
633	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
634	                return
635	            self._reply_receipt(200, receipt)
636	
637	        def _handle_get(self) -> None:
638	            kind, segment = self._route()
639	            if kind is None:
640	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
641	                return
642	            if kind == "collection":
643	                # The tenant-scoped, paginated listing of accepted
644	                # requests; read-only like the item observations.
645	                self._serve_list()
646	                return
647	            # item (acceptance receipt), status and execution_log are the
648	            # three GET-only reads; authorization/tenant/id resolution and
649	            # the resulting error ordering are shared by all of them.
650	            assert segment is not None
651	            resolved = self._resolve_read(segment)
652	            if resolved is None:
653	                return
654	            tenant_id, request_id = resolved
655	            if kind == "item":
656	                self._serve_receipt(tenant_id, request_id)
657	            elif kind == "status":
658	                self._serve_status(tenant_id, request_id)
659	            else:
660	                self._serve_execution_log(tenant_id, request_id)
661	
662	        def _resolve_read(self, segment: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
663	            """Authorize and resolve ``(tenant_id, request_id)`` for a GET.
664	
665	            Returns ``None`` after already replying. Authentication runs
666	            before request-id validation and storage; with auth enabled the
667	            full tenant authorization completes before the id shape is even
668	            inspected, while the unauthenticated contract keeps its
669	            historical id-shape-before-tenant order.
670	            """
671	            principal = self._authorize(_ROLE_READ)
672	            if principal is None:
673	                return None
674	            if auth is not None:
675	                # With auth enabled the full authorization -- including
676	                # resolving the target tenant and matching it -- completes
677	                # before request-id syntax is even inspected, so a foreign
678	                # principal cannot reach id validation or storage.
679	                try:
680	                    tenant_id = self._tenant_id()
681	                except _BadRequest:
682	                    self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
683	                    return None
684	                if not self._tenant_allowed(principal[0], tenant_id):
685	                    return None
686	                try:
687	                    request_id = _normalize_request_id(segment)
688	                except _BadRequest:
689	                    # Unknown and malformed ids share one outcome.
690	                    self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
691	                    return None
692	            else:
693	                # Unauthenticated contract keeps its historical order:
694	                # request-id shape is checked before the tenant header.
695	                try:
696	                    request_id = _normalize_request_id(segment)
697	                except _BadRequest:
698	                    self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
699	                    return None
700	                try:
701	                    tenant_id = self._tenant_id()
702	                except _BadRequest:
703	                    self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
704	                    return None
705	            return tenant_id, request_id
706	
707	        def _serve_receipt(self, tenant_id: str, request_id: str) -> None:
708	            try:
709	                record = store.get(tenant_id, request_id)
710	            except RequestNotFound:
711	                # Missing ids and cross-tenant lookups are indistinguishable.
712	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
713	                return
714	            except ValueError:
715	                self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
716	                return
717	            except _StorageUnavailable:
718	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
719	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
720	                return
721	            except (sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError, OSError):
722	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
723	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
724	                return
725	            self._reply_receipt(200, record)
726	
727	        def _serve_status(self, tenant_id: str, request_id: str) -> None:
728	            try:
729	                record = store.get_status(tenant_id, request_id)
730	            except RequestNotFound:
731	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
732	                return
733	            except ValueError:
734	                self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
735	                return
736	            except _StorageUnavailable:
737	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
738	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
739	                return
740	            except (sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError, OSError):
741	                # Corrupt persisted rows surface as fixed-text RuntimeErrors.
742	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
743	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
744	                return
745	            self._reply_status(record)

747	        def _serve_execution_log(self, tenant_id: str, request_id: str) -> None:
748	            try:
749	                attempts = store.get_execution_log(tenant_id, request_id)
750	            except RequestNotFound:
751	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
752	                return
753	            except ValueError:
754	                self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
755	                return
756	            except _StorageUnavailable:
757	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)

767	        def _serve_list(self) -> None:
768	            # The tenant-scoped listing shares the read endpoints'
769	            # authorization and tenant resolution: authentication first,
770	            # then the tenant (header or query) and its match against the
771	            # principal, then query-parameter validation, then storage.
772	            principal = self._authorize(_ROLE_READ)
773	            if principal is None:
774	                return
775	            try:
776	                tenant_id = self._tenant_id()
777	            except _BadRequest:
778	                self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
779	                return
780	            if not self._tenant_allowed(principal[0], tenant_id):
781	                return
782	            try:
783	                filters = self._list_filters()
784	            except _BadRequest:
785	                self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
786	                return
787	            try:
788	                page = store.list_requests(tenant_id, **filters)
789	            except ValueError:
790	                # The store's fixed-text listing ValueError covers every
791	                # invalid filter, limit or cursor shape.
792	                self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
793	                return
794	            except _StorageUnavailable:
795	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
796	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
797	                return
798	            except (sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError, OSError):
799	                # Corrupt persisted rows surface as fixed-text OSErrors.
800	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
801	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
802	                return
803	            self._reply_listing(page)

805	        def _list_filters(self) -> dict[str, object]:
806	            """Validate the listing query string into store arguments.
807	
808	            Only ``tenant_id``, ``status``, ``created_from``,
809	            ``created_to``, ``cursor`` and ``limit`` may appear, each at
810	            most once (``tenant_id`` keeps its historical
811	            header-or-query resolution in ``_tenant_id``). ``status`` is
812	            a comma-separated list of distinct lifecycle statuses. Every
813	            other shape is a bad request; the store re-validates the
814	            values themselves as defence in depth.
815	            """
816	            params = parse_qs(urlsplit(self.path).query, keep_blank_values=True)
817	            if not set(params) <= _LIST_QUERY_PARAMS:
818	                raise _BadRequest("unknown query parameter")
819	            filters: dict[str, object] = {}
820	            for name in ("status", "created_from", "created_to", "cursor", "limit"):
821	                values = params.get(name)
822	                if values is None:
823	                    continue
824	                if len(values) != 1:
825	                    raise _BadRequest(f"duplicate {name}")
826	                value = values[0]
827	                if name == "status":
828	                    filters["statuses"] = self._parse_status_filter(value)
829	                elif name == "limit":
830	                    # Far more digits than the 1..1000 domain can ever
831	                    # hold is a bad request, not a storage fault (and an
832	                    # unbounded digit string must never reach int()).
833	                    if not _LIST_LIMIT_RE.match(value) or len(value) > 10:
834	                        raise _BadRequest("invalid limit")
835	                    filters["limit"] = int(value)
836	                elif not value:
837	                    raise _BadRequest(f"invalid {name}")
838	                else:
839	                    filters[name] = value
840	            return filters
841	
842	        def _parse_status_filter(self, value: str) -> list[str]:
843	            if not value:
844	                raise _BadRequest("invalid status")
845	            statuses = value.split(",")
846	            if any(status not in _REQUEST_STATUSES for status in statuses):
847	                raise _BadRequest("invalid status")
848	            if len(set(statuses)) != len(statuses):
849	                raise _BadRequest("duplicate status")
850	            return statuses
851	
852	        # -- input parsing ---------------------------------------------
853	
854	        def _tenant_id(self) -> str:
855	            header = self.headers.get(_TENANT_HEADER)
856	            if header is not None:
857	                tenant = header.strip()
858	                if tenant:
859	                    return tenant
860	            query = parse_qs(urlsplit(self.path).query).get("tenant_id")
861	            if query:
862	                tenant = query[-1].strip()
863	                if tenant:
864	                    return tenant
865	            raise _BadRequest("missing tenant")
866	
867	        def _read_json_object(self) -> dict:
868	            body = self._read_body()
869	            try:
870	                parsed = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))
871	            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
872	                raise _BadRequest("invalid json body")
873	            if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
874	                raise _BadRequest("body must be a JSON object")
875	            return parsed
876	
877	        def _read_body(self) -> bytes:
878	            raw_length = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
879	            if raw_length is None:
880	                raise _BadRequest("missing content length")
881	            try:
882	                length = int(raw_length)
883	            except (TypeError, ValueError):
884	                raise _BadRequest("invalid content length")
885	            if length < 0 or length > _MAX_BODY_BYTES:
886	                # Leave the oversized tail unread and close the
887	                # connection so keep-alive cannot desync the next request.
888	                self.close_connection = True
889	                raise _BadRequest("body too large")
890	            try:
891	                return self.rfile.read(length)
892	            except OSError:
893	                raise _BadRequest("unreadable body")

895	        # -- responses --------------------------------------------------
896	
897	        def _reply_receipt(self, status: int, receipt: dict[str, str]) -> None:
898	            if set(receipt) != {"request_id", "status", "created_at"}:
899	                # Corrupt persisted rows must never be presented as a
900	                # receipt.
901	                raise RuntimeError("malformed receipt from store")
902	            body = (
903	                json.dumps(
904	                    {
905	                        "request_id": receipt["request_id"],
906	                        "status": receipt["status"],
907	                        "created_at": receipt["created_at"],
908	                    },
909	                    ensure_ascii=False,
910	                    separators=(",", ":"),
911	                )
912	                + "\n"
913	            ).encode("utf-8")
914	            self._write_body(status, body)
915	
916	        def _reply_status(self, record: dict[str, str]) -> None:
917	            # The current-status record has the identical fixed shape and
918	            # field order as the acceptance receipt; only the status value
919	            # differs. Reuse the same strict renderer.
920	            self._reply_receipt(200, record)

922	        def _reply_execution_log(
923	            self, request_id: str, attempts: list[dict[str, object]]
924	        ) -> None:
925	            if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
926	                raise RuntimeError("malformed execution log from store")
